answer: No, your records show no blood clot in your lung. The scan you remember was a CT angiogram of your chest on 8 July 2025. Its report says there was no pulmonary embolism (a clot in the lung), that your lungs were clear, and that there was no fluid around the lungs or heart. The report also noted mild wear-and-tear changes in the thoracic spine. Your doctors later recorded the possible lung clot as ruled out, and the problem they treated that summer was chest wall pain, which resolved. A blood test taken the same day (D-dimer) was mildly high. That test is sensitive but not specific, so a high result alone does not mean a clot, and the scan found none. If you still have chest pain, shortness of breath or leg swelling, tell your doctor promptly, as these need checking whatever the old result.
short: CT angiogram of the chest on 2025-07-08 showed no pulmonary embolism; the lung clot was ruled out. A same-day D-dimer was mildly high, which is nonspecific.
